title: Für Elise, WoO 59 (arranged, full A-B-A-C-A form)
subtitle: Each section written out once - our own abridged arrangement, not a full published edition's length
trains: The rondo's full shape in miniature: the A theme, a lyrical F-major episode, an agitated C section with wide leaps, and the fast 32nd-note broken-chord run that puts this arrangement past Intermediate's reach.

provenance.author: Musicanyya practice material
provenance.basedOn: Beethoven, Für Elise, WoO 59 (public domain, c. 1810). Cross-checked against Mutopia Project piece-info id 931, fur_Elise_WoO59.ly (typeset by Stelios Samelis). A theme reuses fur-elise-theme.musicxml's already-reviewed pitches.
provenance.note: See limitations for a full, itemised disclosure of which passages were independently source-checked (form, key/metre, the A theme, and the famous run's exact shape) versus reconstructed from general knowledge (bridges, B section, the C-section bass-octave opening). Re-checked 2026-09-22 (later session): downloaded and visually inspected the Mutopia Project's complete published PDF engraving directly (fur_Elise_WoO59-let.pdf, piece-info id 931/2059, typeset by Stelios Samelis, 102 written measures) rather than relying on the earlier excerpt-only fetch. Confirmed the overall form (A-B-A-C-A with 1st/2nd-ending bridges), 3/8 metre, A minor with no key signature, Poco moto tempo marking, the pp opening dynamic, and the ottava-marked 32nd-note run in the C section all match this file. No machine-readable LilyPond source is published for this piece (unlike the Chopin Op. 28 items in this same wave, which were verified pitch-by-pitch against literal LilyPond source text), so a full mechanical note-by-note cross-check of the still-flagged passages (bridges, B-section melody, C-section bass-octave opening) was not performed this session; those items remain honest reconstructions, not verified transcriptions, exactly as disclosed below.

limitations: Independently checked against Mutopia's fur_Elise_WoO59.ly (piece-info id 931): A minor with no key signature throughout, including the F-major episode (written with accidentals, not a key change, matching that source) - 3/8 metre; the A theme's own internal repeat-like structure (bars 1-4 restated as 5-8, reused from fur-elise-theme.musicxml); and the exact note sequence of the famous fast run (ascending broken-chord arpeggios through three registers ending in a chromatic descending cascade in 32nds, mm 41-45), checked against a verbatim excerpt of that source.

NOT independently verified note-by-note against the primary source (the available tools could fetch-and-summarize short excerpts only, not download/OCR the full score): the connective bridges (mm 9-10, 19-20, 29-30, 46-47), the B-section melody (mm 11-18), and the C-section's alternating-bass-octave opening (mm 31-40). These were composed by the author from strong general knowledge of this very well-known work, kept diatonically and harmonically conservative, but are a good-faith reconstruction, not a verified transcription. Recommend checking against an IMSLP facsimile or the Mutopia PDF bar-by-bar before this item is treated as fully verified.

Shorter than a full published edition (59 written measures + pickup vs. roughly 120-140 in print): each formal section (A-B-A-C-A) is written out once, complete, rather than padded with additional unverified repetition/figuration some editions include.
